title: The Role of Leveraged ETFs and Option Market Imbalances on End-of-Day Price Dynamics
one_line: Leveraged-ETF rebalancing creates market-wide end-of-day momentum, while options delta-hedging can either amplify or reverse the day's move depending on dealers' inventory; both pressures are mechanical and reverse at the next open.

findings.statement: Leveraged ETF rebalancing and delta hedging create large price pressure in the last part of the day.
findings.evidence: Options holdings 2010-2020, CBOE/NASDAQ open interest by investor type.

findings.statement: LETFs drive market-wide momentum into the close; delta hedging stabilizes or amplifies depending on prior return and dealer inventory.
Both effects reverse quickly at the next day's open.
Combining both mechanisms improves prediction of the last-30-minute direction.

why.pattern: Execution mechanics of forced rebalancers (LETFs, option hedgers) near the close.
why.mechanism: LETFs must buy after up days and sell after down days at the close; dealers hedge gamma.

reported_results.headline: Close-time momentum from LETFs; reversal next open.

tradable_edge: Supports noise_area_last_half_hour_es; adds a next-morning reversal angle (fade the last-30-minute move at the next open).
angles: Next-open reversal of a large last-30-minute move
